thread:
Maya (oncall): Alert — hosted-us-west GPU admission queue spiked at ~18:02 UTC, hosted API 502/503s increasing. Paging infra/SRE.
Maya (oncall): Reproducing symptoms: long queues, admission controller logs full, fallback routing kicking to us-east.
AlertBot: [ALERT] hosted-us-west: admission_queue_length > 400 (avg 6m) — triggered at 2026-01-14T18:02:10Z
Samir (infra): Acknowledged. grabbing logs and runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/admission
Jordan (eng-runtime): Seeing many long-context generate calls (seq_len > 8k) from a small set of customers, KV cache misses high. That pushed per-request GPU time way up.
Priya (eng-ml): Which model variants? long-context for rerank/longform?
Jordan (eng-runtime): Mostly open-rankers + custom quantized variants; tail requests amplified compute by ~4x.
Lee (sre): Confirmed application-level 502s correlate with admission rejections + downstream timeouts. us-east saw a surge after fallback policy started routing.
Samir (infra): I'm going to limit cross-region fallback while we triage. Applying emergency guard:
Samir (infra): ```bash
# emergency: cap fallback concurrency to 150
curl -s -X POST \"https://admin.internal/route-config\" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"fallback_concurrency_cap":150}'
```
Maya (oncall): Done. early signal — us-east fallback inflow fell ~30% after that.
Jordan (eng-runtime): Rolling back the recent admission estimator rollout (the one that overestimates capacity for mixed-seq workloads). Patch going out now.
Jordan (eng-runtime): ```yaml
# admission config change applied
admission_estimator: v1.3.1 -> v1.2.8 (rollback)
pool_reserved_percent: 0.2
max_tokens_in_flight_per_pool: 1_200_000
```
Priya (eng-ml): Also saw a burst of reranks from a partner's batch job starting at 18:00. They didn't show in spike detection because their requests looked "valid" but were long. Need per-customer long-seq throttle.
Lee (sre): Can we throttle by sequence length? even a simple rule: if seq_len>6k, cap concurrency to 8 per-customer.
Jordan (eng-runtime): Yep, will add a temporary admission rule for long-seq. Patching now.
Jordan (eng-runtime): ```json
{"admission_rules": [{"predicate": "seq_len>6000", "max_concurrency_per_identity": 8}]}
```
Samir (infra): Autoscaler logs: we failed to provision new nodes because spot pool was exhausted and on-demand warm-up was delayed by 6m. Need better warm pool strategy for bursty long-run workloads.
Maya (oncall): Summary so far: 1) Long-seq burst from partner + quantized variants => huge per-request GPU time. 2) Admission estimator overpromised capacity. 3) Fallback routing overloaded us-east. 4) Autoscaler didn't spin capacity fast enough.
Priya (eng-ml): Impact: estimated extra GPU-hours ~120 over 3h -> cost delta ~ $12k (prelim). Also customer-facing SLO hits for hosted API.
Lee (sre): Current status: queues stabilizing after rollback + fallback cap + long-seq throttle. Error rate trending down. Monitoring 30m for regressions.
Samir (infra): Immediate follow-ups I will own: enforce warm-on-demand pool with 10% reserved for spikes, add spot pool fallback health check, improve scaling cooldowns.
Jordan (eng-runtime): My follow-ups: permanent admission rule for long-seq, add sequence-length-aware estimator, add unit tests for mixed-seq workloads.
Priya (eng-ml): I'll create a synthetic workload (mixed seq lengths, quantized variants) and add to CI eval harness.
Lee (sre): I'll draft a short incident timeline and SLO impact spreadsheet. We'll have a postmortem doc template ready by EOD.
Maya (oncall): Owners set: Samir -> infra guardrails, Jordan -> estimator rollback + tests, Priya -> synthetic tests, Lee -> incident doc.
Maya (oncall): Immediate mitigation closed, watch window until 19:30 UTC. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Samir (infra): one more note — network egress to us-east peaked and triggered an unexpected quota on our inter-region bandwidth, that added ~1m of routing delays. I'll open a quota request with cloud team.
Jordan (eng-runtime): We'll also add a soft cap on cross-region fallback concurrency (config-only, not a hard block) and a circuit breaker so a single region won't domino others.
Priya (eng-ml): Suggest adding alerting for "long-tail per-identity GPU time" so we can catch sustained heavy hitters earlier.
Lee (sre): Agreed. I'll add that alert to the monitoring runbook and tune thresholds with Priya.
Maya (oncall): Thanks — we'll convert this thread to a postmortem draft in incidents/ after the watch window. Recording notes here so we capture the immediate timeline.
Maya (oncall): Timeline (brief): 18:00 partner batch starts -> 18:02 admission queue spike -> 18:05 fallback to us-east -> 18:08 autoscaler warm-up fails -> 18:12 emergency guard + rollback applied -> 18:20 error rate backtrending down.
Jordan (eng-runtime): Adding to followups: run a chaos test (simulate long-seq flood) against Dedicated and Hosted to validate guardrails.
Samir (infra): I'll also add cost alert for >$6k abnormal spend in 3h window so we see these financial spikes earlier.
Maya (oncall): Closing thread for now — reopening if error rate reappears. Good triage, quick reactions. We'll keep owners posted on the formal postmortem.
